description: Plug and play, as a .NET developer starts: the dotnet new templates make a solution of a C# app, an asm library and xunit tests that builds without warnings, runs and tests with no RID, global.json pin or hand-written entry. dotnet sln add takes a new .asmproj, dotnet add reference still refuses one (a .NET CLI limit with target framework aliases), and the hand-written ProjectReference it asks for works; the static library template links into an asm program, and what leaves the machine says so: a portable publish and a pack warn ASM0013, a publish for one RID does not. The folder's own global.json, Directory.Build.props and Directory.Packages.props stand for a user's fresh folder (empty, but for NuGet's audit, which is off): the projects name their SDK version inline, and nothing of tests/scenarios' settings reaches them.

steps.description: Installs the templates under test from the local feed, into this scenario's own CLI home (DOTNET_CLI_HOME), never the developer's profile: the package lands there.
A solution: Demo.App (C#), Demo.Native (asm) and Demo.Tests (xunit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, which the template sets in the folder's global.json). Its restore post action restores all three.
The solution build builds the asm library for this machine (no RuntimeIdentifiers listed) and delivers it to the app.
The app calls the asm function through the C# binding the SDK writes from the template's PROTO line (Demo.Native.Add.AddInts): no [LibraryImport] written.
The template's five tests of the asm function, through Microsoft.Testing.Platform.
A second asm library, into the solution's folder.
dotnet sln add takes an .asmproj: the SDK's DefaultProjectTypeGuid gives it the generic project type (0.3.0 printed an unknown project type and added nothing).
The added project builds with the solution.

Still refused: the .NET CLI parses the referenced project's TargetFramework text, and freestanding is an alias it does not know (NuGet and the build accept it; dotnet/sdk#57317, tracked in AsmFoundation/AsmSdk#5). The docs show the one-line ProjectReference instead; this step fails once the CLI accepts it, and then the step, the docs and issue #5 change.
stderr: cannot be added due to incompatible targeted frameworks

steps.description: What the docs say to do instead: CallsExtra (written by hand, in this folder) has the one ProjectReference line to the asmlib template's library, and calls its add_ints through the binding the SDK writes from the template's PROTO line (Demo.Extra.Add.AddInts).
A portable publish carries the library of the one RID it was built for, and says so.
So does a pack of the RID-less library.
A publish for one RID asks for that RID's build: nothing to warn about.
The published app runs on its own, the library next to it.
dotnet run builds the asm program for this machine and runs it.
The static library builds for this machine.
The static library in use: UsesShared (an asm program written by hand, in this folder) references Shared, includes its Shared.inc and returns mul_ints(6, 7) from main.
